title: Regional drain blackhole exposed fallback variant oscillation: incident retrospective and durable fixes
creator: Ava Chen
summary: During a routine regional capacity drain for planned maintenance, a combination of an aggregator regression and an autoscaler heartbeat mismatch produced a near-zero egress weight for us-west-2. The control plane treated that as a hard drain (blackhole) instead of gradual, which caused smart-routing to rapidly push traffic to lower-tier variants. Those variants started to hit their own capacity/post-failure behaviors, triggering cascading fallbacks and an oscillation between model variants across multiple regions. This incident impacted hosted API customers in NA for ~42 minutes, increasing P50 latency and per-token costs and causing several app-layer timeouts for downstream customers.
impact_summary: ~42 minute regional outage window affecting ~8% of production requests (primarily us-west-2 customers). P50 latency increased 3.1x, error rate spiked to 7.8% on routed paths that hit fallbacks. Some customers saw degraded structured output caused by variant differences. No customer data was exposed.
timeline: 2026-02-10T09:03:18Z - Control plane scheduled planned maintenance window for us-west-2 (non-user-visible), intent: drain 25% of GPUs to run kernel update.

2026-02-10T09:11:42Z - Regional aggregator service (signal-agg) returned malformed weight vector due to a recent change in decay math (PR #6229). One entry for us-west-2 evaluated to -0.000012 which got clamped to 0 by downstream logic.
2026-02-10T09:12:05Z - Routing controller observed egress_weight==0 and transitioned region to DRAIN_IMMEDIATE state instead of DRAIN_GRADUAL due to an unexpected null-check path.

2026-02-10T09:12:30Z - Smart router re-evaluated bucket allocations: high-volume traffic for a number of enterprise customers was redistributed to fallback variant family (v-small, quantized), which had tighter per-host concurrency.

2026-02-10T09:21:00Z - Fallback variant hosts started returning capacity_exhausted and 502 errors. Control plane began promoting additional fallback instances in other regions; autoscaler backpressure signals produced another negative feedback loop.
2026-02-10T09:36:00Z - Observability alerts (routing-error-rate, cross-region-latency) triggered and SRE began mitigation.

2026-02-10T09:43:13Z - Emergency mitigation: temporarily pinned routing policy to prefer regional affinity and disabled immediate-drain transition rule (hotfix patch deployed: runtime-1.29-hotfix-02).
2026-02-10T09:54:05Z - Traffic started to rebalance toward healthy hosts; error rates trended back to baseline by 09:56Z.
2026-02-10T10:05:00Z - Incident declared resolved and customer incident message posted.
2026-02-10T11:30:00Z - Post-incident investigation kickoff with runtime, routing, and telemetry teams.

2026-02-24T15:00:00Z - Fixes merged: PR #6268 (clamp/validation for aggregator output), PR #6279 (explicit DRAIN_GRADUAL enforcement), PR #6293 (autoscaler heartbeat robustness), PR #6311 (routing circuit-breaker for fallback flood). Deployed to staging and gradually to production over 2026-02-26 to 2026-02-28 under runtime-1.29.
2026-03-02T10:00:00Z - Postmortem review and cross-team signoff completed. Action items tracked and scheduled.
root_cause: A regression in the regional signal aggregator changed the decay formula such that transient negative rounding errors produced a near-zero weight for us-west-2. The routing controller lacked a defensive check for 'effective zero' vs explicit drained state and interpreted this as a hard drain. Smart-routing's immediate-drain path redistributed high-volume user traffic to lower-capacity fallback variants. Those fallback hosts produced capacity failures, and autoscaler backpressure signals amplified the redistribution (feedback loop). Two gaps surfaced: missing validation/clamping in signal-agg and an aggressive immediate-drain transition in the routing controller.
contributing_factors: recent change to decay math in signal-agg (PR #6229) was insufficiently fuzz-tested against edge rounding
routing controller had a code path that treated weight==0 as unconditional drain without hysteresis
fallback variants were provisioned with lower per-host concurrency and did not have fast autoscale headroom for sudden spikes
observability thresholds for early-warning anomaly detection were tuned too wide for immediate-drain transitions, delaying human response
no routing circuit-breaker existed to limit rate of variant promotions during a cross-region surge
mitigations_applied_during_incident: hotfix: temporarily disable immediate-drain transition rule (runtime-1.29-hotfix-02)
pin routing policy to regional-affinity to reduce cross-region blast radius
manually increased capacity for fallback variant family in eu-central-1 and us-east-1 to absorb overflow
increased alerting sensitivity on routing egress-weight deltas and fallback activation rate
long_term_fixes: Add validation/clamping and unit/fuzz tests around decay math in signal-agg (merged PR #6268)
Enforce DRAIN_GRADUAL by default and require explicit override to go to DRAIN_IMMEDIATE; add hysteresis gates (PR #6279)
Introduce routing circuit-breaker to cap rate of variant promotions per rolling window and fallback flood damping (PR #6311)
Increase baseline autoscaler headroom for fallback variants and add temporary burst pool option (PR #6293)
Improve telemetry: new metric routing.egress_weight_delta_1m and alert runbook for >30% delta in <2m
Add a replay test in staging that simulates planned drain + 10% traffic spike against fallback variants
Document runbook changes and run a quarterly chaos-drain exercise in staging

followups_and_tracking: Action items have been created in Linear and linked to this parent issue ENG-341900. Progress will be tracked in the Smart Routing Resilience project board. Quarterly chaos-drain exercises will be scheduled starting 2026-Q2. SLA impact assessment for affected customers completed and appropriate credits processed by CS.
lessons_learned: Defense-in-depth for signals: never trust a single numeric output without validation and hysteresis. Routing decisions that move traffic across regions must include rate-limiting and circuit-breakers to avoid second-order failures. Fallback variants should be treated as elastic shock absorbers, not full-capacity replacements; ensure autoscaler and burst capacity are aligned with expected worst-case failovers.
postmortem_review_notes: PM review: Agreed that DRAIN_IMMEDIATE default is too risky for non-critical maintenance
Design review: Need clearer annotation on variant compatibility guarantees and visible diffs when a fallback is used
Security review: No findings; encryption and audit logs intact
SRE review: Runbook updated and added clear escalation thresholds
